suppressions.candidate: NOT NULL role constraint could reject pre-existing admin accounts
suppressions.note: The migration first adds role as nullable, backfills every null role to admin at line 27, and only then adds the role check and NOT NULL constraint at lines 28-29. This is the ordered compatibility window required by task_01.md:24-26 and :51.

suppressions.candidate: Existing users could be deactivated during the additive account migration
suppressions.note: Adding ativo with DEFAULT true NOT NULL makes the existing row state and the new-record default agree with task_01.md:25-26. The migration changes neither IDs, emails, password hashes, nor applications.decided_by references.

suppressions.candidate: A failed multi-statement migration could leave a partial schema
suppressions.note: The configured postgres-js Drizzle migrator executes each pending migration inside one transaction before recording it in drizzle.__drizzle_migrations (node_modules/drizzle-orm/pg-core/dialect.js:56-71), so any failing statement rolls back the migration rather than publishing a partial 0006 state.

suppressions.candidate: New foreign keys and indexes could remove or invalidate existing application data
suppressions.note: application_observations and issued_documents are newly created empty tables before their foreign keys and indexes are added. The migration does not recreate, delete from, or alter applications or existing application references; the only altered existing table is admin_users, handled by the preceding ordered backfill.

suppressions.candidate: Generated snapshot might not represent the SQL migration
suppressions.note: The generated snapshot records the same role check, new tables, foreign keys, uniqueness constraint, and indexes named by 0006 and lib/db/schema.ts. It is migration metadata rather than an independently owned executable implementation.
